evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."

The contract exposes "object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs, readings and ordered named role players, direct subtype links and registered constraint signatures" -- no completeness or subset marker is among the exposed fields.

"The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence." Full/partial status is a host-side record; the plan never states it is communicated to the consuming agent, yet Section 5 also demands "A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty."

"a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral" exercises retry after a miss, but no listed check asserts the agent was told the supplied context was partial.

concerns.recommendation: State where the subset indicator lives for whoever reads the prompt (a field in the versioned view, or a preamble mandated by the packaged host protocol guide), and add a GC2 acceptance criterion that an include-backed partial view is explicitly marked as not full.
concerns.title: Subset guidance requirement has no agent-visible artifact feature or falsifiable check

evidence.observation: "Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline." ... "Use a view digest for replay." The canonicalization rules (key ordering, separators, unicode escaping, number formatting) and whether the version marker is embedded in the artifact are unstated.

The only byte-stability evidence is "deterministic bytes" and "CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel" -- both run in one environment on one wheel, so cross-platform or cross-version canonicalization drift that changes replay digests would pass.

concerns.recommendation: Pin the canonicalization profile by name or documented house rules, state whether "Version 1" travels inside the artifact, and derive the view digest from exactly those rules so replay identity is well defined.
concerns.title: Canonical JSON form and version marker are named but not pinned, weakening digest replay

evidence.observation: "Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale."
"Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure." -- a control, but assigned to no phase.

The GC1 verify list covers "complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits" -- no check that excluded fields are absent from compact output.

concerns.recommendation: Schedule the sentinel test inside GC1: inject marker strings into author evidence, samples, notes and rationale on the fixture and assert they do not appear in the compact bytes.
concerns.title: Disclosure-exclusion control is described but not scheduled as a falsifiable check

evidence.observation: "Use a view digest for replay. Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest."
"evidence-only edits" appears as a verify topic with no expected outcome (digest unchanged AND evolution still gated, or something else).

"Existing evolution preview and apply perform stale-state checks." -- pin verification is attributed to existing machinery even though the compact view digest is a new surface; whether those existing checks already verify "verified transitive include pins" is not evidenced.

concerns.recommendation: Spell out the fixture outcome (view digest identical, evolution still blocked on root-byte or transitive-pin mismatch) and confirm or extend the existing stale-state checks so verified transitive include pins are covered on the compact path.
concerns.title: Evidence-only-edit and include-pin evolution gating has no stated expected outcome

evidence.observation: "Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context, stable identifiers and explicit guidance when a host supplies a subset."
"Loader checks protect composed ID identity." -- asserted, with no cited test.
"Verify complete identifiers on fixtures" checks completeness of identifiers, not their stability across edits, even though composed IDs can change when their inputs change.

concerns.recommendation: Add a GC1 fixture asserting identifiers are unchanged under an evidence-only edit and change only in the documented way under a targeted rename, so "stable identifiers" has stated falsifiable evidence.
concerns.title: Stable-identifiers obligation rests on an asserted loader control with no stability test

evidence.observation: "Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture." No expected relation or bound is stated, so the comparison cannot fail.
"Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture." -- measurement is confined but no direction or threshold is declared for the milestone's namesake property.

concerns.recommendation: State the expected relation on the fixture (compact strictly fewer bytes than ordinary review output, or a recorded ratio threshold), or explicitly record compactness as measured-but-unclaimed alongside the Section 9 limitations.
concerns.title: Compactness byte comparison lacks an acceptance criterion

evidence.observation: "Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere." Which sequences besides role players are "meaningful", and what sort key orders everything else, are unstated.
"role order" and "deterministic bytes" are verified, but a silent re-sort of a meaningful sequence or insertion-order leakage would still pass single-machine determinism tests.

concerns.recommendation: Enumerate the meaningfully ordered sequences and the deterministic sort key per element kind in the versioned format description, so ordering is a format rule rather than an implementation accident.
concerns.title: Meaningful-versus-deterministic ordering rules are not enumerated

response.summary: Digest matched. The two-phase plan states implementable obligations with mostly concrete falsification (deterministic bytes, installed-wheel CLI/API parity, unchanged default output, retry-after-miss via role players, ambiguous deferral), but the issue-295 subset-guidance requirement has no agent-visible artifact feature or acceptance criterion, and several named controls (canonical JSON profile, disclosure sentinels, evidence-only evolution gating, composed-ID stability) lack scheduled, outcome-bearing checks.
